findings.label: The 1.71 ms long-scan case is device kernel time and 98.5% of it is the AIV scalar pipeline
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary; AI_VECTOR_CORE task, aic* counters are 0 because no cube kernel is involved

evidence.metric: Task Start Time delta between consecutive invocations vs Task Duration (host launch gap)

findings.inference: Only one kernel runs per iteration (operation_count=1) and its measured device duration 1711.201 us is 99.84% of the eval latency 1.713889 ms, so the 1.71 ms is device time, not host/launch overhead: the gap between consecutive task starts is under 1 us and Task Wait Time is ~0.0-0.2 us, i.e. the device queue is saturated. Inside the kernel the AIV breakdown is scalar 1684.47 us (98.5%), vector 9.85 us (0.6%), MTE2 10.75 us (0.6%), MTE3 5.95 us (0.3%). Loads and stores are therefore almost free and the elementwise (a+b)*0.5 is negligible; the time goes to a per-element serial sequence. The only per-element serial construct in the seed source (main.py lines 45-48) is tl.cumsum(t, axis=0) over BLOCK=4096 per program with grid=1024, so the scan is executing as a scalar accumulation chain rather than a vector prefix-sum.

findings.label: Scalar scan cost tracks only the number of scanned elements: identical across dtype, layout and grid size
findings.backend_detail: Output element counts are (N-1)*outer*inner from the frozen specs: 1023*128=130944 and 4095*1024=4193280

evidence.metric: aiv_scalar_time_us per 130944 output elements (fp16 [1024,128] dim=0, stride 128)
aiv_scalar_time_us per 130944 output elements (fp32 [1024,128] dim=0, stride 128)

findings.inference: Normalizing scalar time by output elements gives 506 ns/kelem (timing-0), 402 ns/kelem (timing-1), 514 ns/kelem (timing-2) and 514 ns/kelem (timing-8), i.e. 1945-2490 scanned elements per microsecond of scalar time across two layouts and three dtypes. A vectorized prefix sum scales with log2(N) vector steps and would show up in aiv_vec; instead the cost is strictly linear in element count and sits on the scalar unit. The identical value in the contiguous [128,1024] case and the strided [1024,128] dim=0 case shows it is a property of the scan lowering, not of memory layout or dtype.

findings.inference: timing-0 and timing-2 touch the same number of output elements (130944) with the same fp16 dtype, but timing-2 costs 239.01 us of device time versus 69.26 us: +121.4 us of vector work, +40.6 us of MTE2 and +19.9 us of MTE3, while the scalar scan is unchanged (66.2 -> 67.3 us). So the strided dim=0 loss is not caused by the scan chain; it is the column access pattern (element stride = inner*itemsize = 256 bytes for fp16) forcing per-element address/descriptor work on the vector unit plus inefficient MTE2 gather. The fp32 version of the same shape is cheaper (164.9 us) because its vector component is nearly half (69.7 vs 121.9 us) although its scalar component is identical, which points at dtype conversion work in the vector path (the seed converts both loads to fp32) rather than at the stride cost alone.

findings.inference: For timing-0 the kernel itself is 69.26 us while the eval latency is 105.586 us, so ~36.3 us (34.4%) of each measured iteration is host dispatch/Python/launch cost that no kernel-body change can remove: even a perfect kernel would be capped near ~36 us plus device time on this harness. The same comparison shows this overhead is irrelevant for the other profiled cases (timing-1: 2.69 us, timing-2: 1.22 us, timing-8: ~0 us), so launch reduction is a secondary, small-case-only lever while the kernel body dominates elsewhere. The 44-65 us Task Wait Time observed under msprof is consistent with the host being the limiter for this small shape, but msprof instrumentation inflates gaps, so the eval-vs-device delta is the number to use.

performance_interpretation: The round-1 baseline geo_mean is 0.3546 (33/33 PASSED) and the loss is not spread evenly. Two regimes exist. (1) Long contiguous scans (timing-1/4/7, all ~1.71 ms, speedups 0.151/0.187/0.185): the time is 99.8% device kernel, and 98.5% of the kernel's AIV active time is on the scalar unit (1684 of 1711 us) while vector, MTE2 and MTE3 together total only 26.5 us. The seed's tl.cumsum(t, axis=0) over BLOCK=4096 per program with grid=1024 is therefore behaving as a per-element serial accumulation, and its cost is linear in scanned elements (402 ns/kelem) rather than logarithmic. The three dtypes are within 0.3% of each other on the eval (1.7139/1.7142/1.7087 ms), so the limit is neither bandwidth nor conversion. (2) Strided dim=0 cases (timing-2/5/8): the scalar scan is still present but only 27-40% of AIV time; the extra cost comes from the vector address path (vec 121.9 us for fp16 versus 0.57 us contiguous at the same element count) and from MTE2 (42.1 vs 1.5 us). For the small contiguous shapes (timing-0/3/6) about a third of the 0.103 ms eval latency is outside the kernel entirely. Consequently the highest-leverage change is to stop paying a scalar per-element chain for the prefix sum; reducing launch overhead or retuning tiles cannot address the 1.71 ms regime at all. The reference implementations reach 0.2585-0.3158 ms on these shapes, so the headroom is algorithmic, not hardware. The frozen hypothesis (baseline establishes latency; the [1024,4096] dim=-1 cases and the strided dim=0 cases dominate the loss) is supported by the measured geo_mean and per-case speedups, but the mechanism differs from a generic memory/scan mix: it is a serial scalar scan for the contiguous cases and a vector/MTE2 address-path penalty for the strided ones.

next_experiment.action_description: Replace the single whole-block tl.cumsum with an explicit two-level blocked scan inside one program per line, keeping every other part of the seed identical: same grid (outer*inner), same strides, same mask k < N-1 and tail handling, same fp32 elementwise increment (a+b)*0.5 computed before the scan, same output dtype/store and same host-side dx multiply. Inside the program: reshape the BLOCK-length increment vector into (R, C) with C = 64 or 128 (R = BLOCK/C, e.g. 4096 -> 32x128), compute the within-row prefix with a cube matmul against a lower-triangular ones matrix of shape (C, C) hoisted as a constant, then prefix the R row totals (a chain of length R only, 32 instead of 4096) and broadcast-add that carry back to each row before the existing tl.store. Keep the current seed kernel intact behind a constexpr/size predicate as a fallback so a compile or numerics failure can be rolled back with one flag.
next_experiment.expected_impact: Directly attacks the measured 98.5% scalar component on timing-1/4/7 (1684 of 1711 us): the serial chain per program shrinks from N-1=4095 scalar steps to R=32, and the intra-row work moves to the cube unit, which is completely idle in all four profiles (cube_utilization_pct = 0, aicore_time_us = 0). Since the measured non-scalar pipelines on timing-1 total only ~26.5 us (vec 9.8 + MTE2 10.7 + MTE3 6.0), the long-scan device time should drop far below the current 1.711 ms toward the 0.2585-0.3158 ms reference band, and it should also remove the ~67 us scalar component from the strided dim=0 cases (27-41% of their AIV time). Expected to move geo_mean well above the 0.3546 baseline; timing-1/4/7 are the primary beneficiaries, timing-2/5/8 secondary.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: Rounding order changes: the current kernel accumulates sequentially while a matmul-based prefix sums up to C terms per element, so the fp32 workloads (rtol/atol 1e-4, required_matched_ratio 1) are the tightest gate; if fp32 correctness fails, restrict the matmul scan to fp16/bf16 and keep the seed path for fp32. NaN/Inf propagation and the masked tail (N-1 not a multiple of C, e.g. N-1=1023 with C=128) must be preserved explicitly. Resource risk: a (C,C) fp32 triangular constant must stay small (C=128 -> 64 KB) or the UB/compile budget may fail as in earlier per-program tile overruns; if compilation fails, halve C. Rollback is a one-line predicate flip back to the round-1 kernel; the round-1 source (solution_sha256 543b3a87ff2ccd251ce9cf8d097e89d3b0204c9c30a79eaca9035c0bedc6bad2) is the known-good fallback.

open_questions: Is the 121.9 us of vector time on timing-2 dtype conversion (fp16 -> fp32 of both operands) or strided address generation? fp32 timing-8 shows 69.7 us of vector time on the same shape, but no instruction listing is available to separate the two.
How much of the scalar time is the cumsum chain versus mask/index bookkeeping? An instruction listing, or a probe kernel that only computes the mask, would separate them.
Would a cube/matmul prefix sum stay inside the fp32 1e-4 tolerance on long chains, given the reference is a sequential cumsum?
